svg.title: Mission Logic · The 11-step process
svg.desc: People and AP reason together through eleven distinct steps, from shaping the need and guiding simulations to interpreting outcomes and learning. The steps run top to bottom. Enter at the first unresolved step. Seven continuous return arrows connect source steps to their destination boxes in separate lanes. Matching letters and colors identify their two ends. The single remaining crossing is drawn as a bridge, not a junction. Every step retrieves from and records to project memory. Conditions beside the source steps explain when each common return applies. Move forward when the next step has what it needs; unresolved questions may remain if they do not prevent that decision. Move from testing to selection when there is enough credible evidence to choose. At any step, wait for information or readiness, with an owner, trigger and deadline. Name the scope of any stop and the person authorized to decide it; stopping one inquiry does not automatically stop other work. Before execution, confirm current readiness and permission. Evaluate specified requirements and the real need, including integrated performance. Judge simulation credibility for the particular decision and retain the distinction between observation and explanation.
svg.text: People and AP reason together: shape the need, explore possibilities, decide, act and learn.
New objective → 1 · Finding → 3 · Ready test → 7 · Authorized + ready work → 9 · Check due → 10
Colored return arrows: follow the complete path

g.text: The person names the need; AP helps clarify it.
Together, set an owner and provisional success criterion.
People add context; AP connects assets and constraints.
Together, check conditions and the supporting evidence.
People and AP examine knowns and unknowns.
Identify the affected decision and who needs the answer.
People set criteria; AP shows the tradeoffs.
Check requirements against the real need in use.
People and AP work back from the outcome and forward
from current conditions; include the current course.
Evaluate the risk of each solution
People and AP assess likelihood, effects and mitigation.
Challenge assumptions; keep unsupported odds uncertain.
People guide tests and simulations; AP compares paths.
Check credibility for this decision and observed results.
An unchosen simulated option remains a prediction.
Select a solution and plan execution
AP explains options; the authorized person chooses.
Agree work, checks, resources, sequence and fallbacks.
People perform authorized work; AP follows results.
Report changes; follow agreed responses or ask the owner.
AP assembles evidence; people check requirements
and integrated performance against the real need in use.
People and AP learn: outcome, explanation or simulation?
Keep evidence, limits and reasons; agree the next check.
Permission to use a lesson is a separate judgment.

svg.text: Wait for useful evidence, access, resources,
Name the owner, trigger and latest useful time to resume.
Resume the assigned step when the trigger arrives.
If the deadline arrives first, reconsider or ask the owner.
Stop with a named scope and decision owner
Name what stops: this inquiry, a work package,
or the whole undertaking. The person authorized
for that scope decides; record who and why.
An objective may be met, withdrawn or unresolved;
an inquiry may end when further effort is not worthwhile.
Keep unknowns; notify affected owners. Other work
continues unless also stopped; standing obligations
One finding can settle a child question and change several next actions. See the supporting views.

g.text: People, resources, access and prerequisites in place?
Current permission and instruction? Named person releases.
If not: wait, use an agreed fallback, or reopen the choice.

g.title: 3 → 1 · Revisit the objective: Discovery shows the objective no longer fits the real need.
6 → 5 · Revise for risk: Risk is unacceptable, or mitigation requires a change to the solution.
7 → 5 · Improve the options: Facts still hold, but the options do not perform well enough.
7 → 3 · Recheck the premise: Testing exposes a missing fact or challenges a key assumption.
10 → 3 · Resolve an unknown: The outcome leaves an uncertainty that matters to the next action.
10 → 8 · Make a fresh choice: Evidence is sufficient to choose, but the next action needs an authorized decision.
9 → 3 · Investigate field change: A field change raises an unresolved question that affects the work. If an agreed response covers it, continue within execution.
